brief: Midterm Democrats won Congress, implying gridlock and more fiscal oversight. Separately, the QRA (Quarterly Refunding Announcement) is becoming as market-moving as an FOMC meeting. With federal debt at $40tn and deficits near 6% of GDP, how Treasury finances borrowing increasingly drives yields and equity valuations. The November QRA left coupon and FRN sizes unchanged, raising $28bn new cash from $125bn of refunding, and did not cut long-bond issuance or cap yields, which the note calls mildly reassuring for the long end and a contributor to this week's bond rally. But the statement dropped "at least" from its "next several quarters" guidance, giving Treasury more flexibility to shift maturity if demand weakens. Treasury now expects to borrow $618bn in Q4 and $800bn in Q1 2027 (TGA rising to $1tn) ahead of another debt-ceiling standoff, and plans roughly $70bn of buybacks plus $25bn for cash management. The note argues this doesn't resolve the fiscal arithmetic: with only a third of US debt maturing within a year versus less than half that abroad, rate shocks pass through faster, so future QRAs will matter more across assets, and the line toward financial repression needs watching.
